headline: Easy-run efficiency continues to hold cleanly through the recent 20 km and 11 km work, but with the crossing under three weeks out, the training still hasn't included loaded-pack or sustained-climbing work resembling what's ahead.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is one of a solidly built endurance base being maintained rather than pushed harder. Running volume across the recent four weeks nearly doubled the prior block, and the easy sessions are sitting comfortably in the lower aerobic bands with controlled heart rates — the efficiency signal that's held for two weeks now remains intact under that added load. Strength has stayed regular, though sessions have trended shorter and lighter in character recently, which reads as sensible given the running volume rather than a drop-off. Daily step counts remain very high even on rest days, so background load is substantial beyond what the tracked sessions show. Sleep has been erratic in duration and the Polar strain figure is implausibly low — neither should shift how the training is read right now.
sections.trends: Year-to-date distance is running well ahead of the same point last year, and the recent build shape is coherent: a volume ramp followed by consolidation with efficiency preserved. That's the right shape for someone heading into a multi-day self-supported effort — durable aerobic capacity accumulated without spikes in intensity. The one gap in the shape is specificity: the trend is all steady time-on-feet, with no recent evidence of the terrain-loaded stress the crossing will actually demand.
sections.threshold: The threshold figure is a single anchor point from early July with no rolling baseline yet, so it's a reference rather than a trend. What matters more for the current focus is that comparable-effort easy runs are being held at lower heart rates than earlier in the block — a practical marker of aerobic improvement that's more relevant to a nine-to-ten-day trail effort than a threshold pace number would be. Treat the threshold value as a placeholder until enough history accumulates to say anything about its direction.
